answer: A bounty bond stops fakes: each identity locks 70 credits on a walnut grove deed. An opal seal binds the deed to its key for hunters. A hunter files a plume-signed challenge; an auditor recounts trees; a fake grove forfeits its bond and pays the hunter 40. One fake costs 105: 70 bond, 35 fee; 1,000 fakes cost 105,000, losing 65,000 on a 40,000 pool. Rented groves fail: deed keys cannot match claimants. Honest agents pay 35 once, keep the bond.
